newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude to trade sideways, but fragile.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude to trade sideways, but fragile.

text.p: NYMEX crude futures were expected to move sideways with the possibility of a small bounce at the open, but many chartists remained cautious about lengthening positions.
April crude closed 59 cents lower at $20.30 a barrel and last traded at $20.46 on ACCESS.

"Of course crude prices are oversold if the classic indicators are relied on, but the door is still open to further losses, possibly after a mild bounce," said Leslie Nicholas, energy analyst at GNI commodity brokers in London.

"The problem is that while many participants feel the markets have done enough, they are wary of stepping in on the buy side, especially end users. Therefore we still favour the short side notwithstanding a mild retracement in early activity today."
Nicholas said there was some talk of NYMEX crude getting as low as $18.50.
Indicators such as Relative Strength Indices (RSI) were close to oversold for most of last week.
The nine and 14-day RSIs stood at 23 and 27 percent at Friday's close.
A Washington-based chartist said there were signs that the market could be nearing the bottom of the recent downside action but he remained cautious.
"Some of my oscillator packages are marginally higher which would suggest we're close to a bottom," said the trader.
If crude were to head higher he saw it aiming at a target of $22. On the downside, he saw support for crude at $20.25 in line with a low of last September and below there at $19.75 and $19.25.
Some chartists pointed to possible support at $20.05 and $19.75 in line with an upside gap on the April contract back in August.
Products were expected to be subdued by the continuing weakness in crude. April heating oil ended 1.15 cent off at 53.44 cents and April gasoline 1.16 cent off at 62.56 cents.
On the gasoline front, some chartists said there were signs it was straining to take off on seasonal factors but the shadow of weak crude appeared to be impeding its progress.
"It doesn't matter how strong gasoline is," said the trader. "If its companions are bearish it will get hold back.
On the bullish side for gasoline he said it had registered higher highs and higher lows for most of last week.
He also noted that gasoline appeared to be nearing completion of a five wave retracement which would imply the market was nearing its bottom.
He noted major support at 61.60 and 60 cents for April gasoline. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
